title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). Sigma is an ordered set carrying a topology, not necessarily Hausdorff. Sigma(1) is the graph of the order and b: Sigma(1) -> Sigma(0) = Sigma is the 'target' projection. The conditions are:
(a) b is proper and a local immersion (local homeomorphism onto its image). Hence the diagonal is open and closed, so Sigma*(1) = Sigma(1) minus the diagonal makes sense.
(b) Each lower set Sigma_{<=x} is a finite totally ordered set.
Sigma*(d) is the space of strict chains x_0 < ... < x_d.

This page.
- The target map b: Sigma*(d) -> Sigma*(0), (x_0<...<x_d) -> x_d, has fibre over x identified with P_d({1,...,N(x)}). This is the set of d-element subsets of the totally ordered finite set Sigma_{<x} (so N(x) should be card Sigma_{<x}).
- So Sigma*(1) over Sigma is a 'relative totally ordered set': a family over Sigma of finite totally ordered sets Sigma_{<x}. Grothendieck proposes to rebuild the whole semi-simplicial system (Sigma*(d)) with its face maps from this relative ordered object. He means the fibrewise nerve, using the canonical simplices of the standard totally ordered sets. A marginal note stresses that all of this is purely order-theoretic, independent of the topological condition (dot).

New topological condition (C). For each x, the local sections given by the local-immersion property associate to each z_alpha in Sigma*(1) over x a germ B_alpha of subspace of Sigma at x (the 'bordant' germs). These germs are required to be mutually transversal and pairwise distinct. Then intersections of some of the B_alpha correspond to points of Sigma*(d) over x, as images of germs of Sigma*(d) at those points.

Modern reading. Locally, Sigma looks like the corner structure of a manifold with corners. The boundary hypersurfaces through a point are transversal, and k-fold corners correspond to k-element sets of faces. The extra feature is that the faces through a point are totally ordered by depth: an 'ordered corner' or iterated-fibration structure. This is what one expects of the 'déploiement' (resolution, unzipping) of a stratified space with conical neighbourhoods. The next page calls it a 'stratification localement cylindrique ordonnée', with Sigma*(1) the space of strata of codimension 1.

The page closes by asserting that the Sigma*(d) and all semi-simplicial maps depend only on Sigma*(1) over Sigma*(0) plus the relative order. The next page immediately corrects this: one also needs the source map s = p_1 : Sigma*(1) -> Sigma, injective on b-fibres and avoiding the diagonal.
errors: Off-by-one ambiguity: if N(x) = card(Sigma_{<=x}), the fibre of Sigma*(d) -> Sigma over x is the set of d-subsets of an (N(x)-1)-element set, not P_d({1..N(x)}). The statement is correct with N(x) = card(Sigma_{<x}), which the handwriting may actually show.

Gap in the final claim. The spaces Sigma*(d) (fibrewise d-subsets) and the face maps that keep the last vertex are determined by the relative totally ordered space Sigma*(1)/Sigma. The face map deleting x_d changes the base point and needs the source map s: Sigma*(1) -> Sigma. Grothendieck himself notices and fixes this on the next page (formula (36)).

Condition (C) is stated only at the level of germs. 'Transversal' for subspaces of a general, possibly non-Hausdorff, topological space is not defined here. Presumably it means a local product (corner-type) structure, but this is left implicit.

ideas.what: Relative nerve: a space over Sigma whose fibres are finite totally ordered sets determines the semi-simplicial space of strict chains, with fibre over x equal to the d-subsets of Sigma_{<x}.
ideas.modern_name: Nerve of a (topological) poset / semi-simplicial space of chains; fibrewise decomposition by target
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Segal, Quillen-style nerves of topological posets/categories)

ideas.what: Condition that the local branches (germs B_alpha) attached to points of Sigma*(1) over x are mutually transversal, with intersections indexed by chains, i.e. by points of Sigma*(d).
ideas.modern_name: Manifold with corners / normal-crossing face structure with totally ordered faces at each point (iterated fibration structure, ordered corners)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Melrose (manifolds with corners, 1990s); Albin-Leichtnam-Mazzeo-Piazza (resolution of Thom-Mather spaces, 2012); Ayala-Francis-Tanaka (unzipping of conically smooth stratified spaces, 2017)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to a theory of stratified spaces/tame topology, but this specific formalism is not, to my knowledge, published

ideas.what: Encoding a locally cylindrical ordered stratification by a tower of spaces Sigma*(d) -> ... -> Sigma*(1) -> Sigma*(0) with source/target maps, i.e. a topological category-like (Segal-type) object built from proper local homeomorphisms.
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path / stratified étale semi-simplicial space; poset-stratified space as a topological category

missed.claim: Grothendieck formalizes the combinatorial skeleton of the 'déploiement' of a stratified space. It is a space over Sigma with proper local-homeomorphic projections whose fibres are finite totally ordered sets, together with a transversality ('corner') condition indexed by chains. This anticipates the 'ordered boundary faces' of the resolution of Thom-Mather spaces into manifolds with corners with iterated fibration structure (ALMP 2012). It also anticipates the 'unzipping' of conically smooth stratified spaces (Ayala-Francis-Tanaka), where depth-ordered faces meet transversally.
missed.quote: les germes B_α bordants de sous-espaces de Σ en x correspondant, par ⊙, aux z_α∈Σ*(1) au-dessus de x ... sont mutuellement transversaux
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents that Grothendieck in 1981-82 was working out a resolution/unzipping theory of stratified spaces with an explicit semi-simplicial encoding of the ordered corner structure. This is relevant to the history of the ALMP and AFT resolution theories, which do not cite these notes.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a working reformulation: a relative nerve plus a transversality-of-branches condition. The math itself is routine, and the overreaching final claim is corrected on the next page. Its interest lies in being an early explicit formalism of ordered corner structures for unfolding stratified spaces, predating ALMP and AFT, but nothing on the page is a striking finished result.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: N(x) is probably defined as card(Σ_{<x}) (strict), consistent with the fibre being P_d({1,...,N(x)}). The handwriting is ambiguous between Σ_{<x} and Σ_{≤x}.
In (C), the inserted word above 'des' is likely 'bordants' (germes B_α bordants de sous-espaces de Σ en x), not 'bandes'.
Left-margin insertion reads approximately: 'tout ceci est indépendant de ⊙ i.e. des propriétés topologiques'.

'semi-simpliciales [soit condition]' — the inserted words above 'correspondant' read approximately 'soit conditions'/'satisfaisant', the sense being 'applications semi-simpliciales correspondant aux simplexes canoniques des tot. ordonnés-types'.
